predictions.prediction_semantics: A prediction of the target, in its unit.

values.note: Each fold receives the mean of the other folds: the reference a model must beat.

cross_validation.note: Every development row is predicted once, by a model fitted on the other folds (the preparation of the variables learnt on those rows too): out-of-fold figures are development evidence, not independent evidence.

params.preprocessing: numeric: median imputation and standardisation; categorical: most frequent imputation and one-hot encoding; fitted on training rows only
params.special_values: numeric special values: indicator column, value imputed; categorical special values: their own category

values.coefficient_scale: target units per standard deviation of the development rows (numeric) or per category (one-hot, not identifiable one by one); associations, not effects

predictions.prediction_semantics: A prediction of the target, in its unit.

preprocessing.note: Parameters learnt, in each fold, on the rows of the other folds and applied to the fold they predict; shown here as learnt on every development row.

cross_validation.note: Every development row is predicted once, by a model fitted on the other folds (the preparation of the variables learnt on those rows too): out-of-fold figures are development evidence, not independent evidence.

values.question: Where are the predictions off, by how much, and does the error grow with the prediction or differ across groups?

smearing.note: The model predicts the target on its own scale (no transform of the target), so no retransformation correction such as Duan's smearing applies. Smearing is not implemented: a log-transformed target would need it.

values.normality_note: The quantile-quantile points compare the standardised residuals with a normal distribution. Normality is not needed for the mean error or the coefficients with this many rows (Lumley et al. 2002); it matters for prediction intervals, which this study does not give.

qq.definition: Quantiles of the residuals standardised by their mean and standard deviation, against the same quantiles of a normal distribution: on a straight diagonal line when the residuals are normal.

by_prediction.binning: 10 equal-count bins of the prediction, in prediction order

heteroscedasticity.rule: Flagged when the rank correlation of the absolute residual with the prediction is at least 0.2 in size, or the residual standard deviation of the top third of the predictions is more than 1.5 times (or less than 1/1.5 of) that of the bottom third
heteroscedasticity.meaning: An error that grows with the prediction makes one interval width wrong for every row; the mean error stays a fair summary.

by_feature.binning: 5 quantile bins of the rows shown
5 quantile bins of the rows shown
5 quantile bins of the rows shown
5 quantile bins of the rows shown

scatter.sampling: 150 rows evenly spaced in prediction order

examples.note: The rows with the largest absolute residuals, with the feature values as written in the file.

point_check.note: The coefficients and their intervals come from the same prepared rows and the same penalised fit.

coefficients.method: Wald intervals, estimate +- z * standard error, from the sandwich covariance H^-1 B H^-1 of the fit on every prepared row (H the penalised information, B the spread of the row scores): the delta-method approximation of a nonparametric bootstrap
coefficients.note: Coefficients of the model fitted on these rows, with Wald intervals from a robust (sandwich) standard error: the approximation of how much each coefficient would move if the rows were drawn again, the preparation of the variables kept as fitted. Associations given the other variables, never effects.
coefficients.scale: target units per standard deviation of the development rows (numeric) or per category (one-hot, not identifiable one by one); associations, not effects

values.note: Development evidence: computed on the out-of-fold predictions of the development rows, on which the model and the rule were chosen. These figures describe the choice; only the final test is independent evidence.

calibration_slope.definition: least-squares slope of the target on the prediction: 1 when the predictions are as spread as the target

linear_checks.method: binned out-of-fold gaps per numeric feature (chi-square, Bonferroni); calibration slope by segment (Cochran's Q); overall calibration slope (Cox 1958)
linear_checks.note: Checks of the candidate linear model on its out-of-fold predictions: a flag is evidence that another model family might follow the data more closely, not proof; choosing a family after seeing it makes that comparison data-contingent.

segments.text: mpg, error-size rank correlation with the prediction
